[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-12.44): Good afternoon, Elaine. Adrian Lim here from the private banking team. I'm calling at the time we arranged. Are you somewhere you can speak privately, or would another time be more convenient?
[seg_0002] Client (12.84-23.19): Hi Adrian. Now is fine, I'm in my office with the door closed. I've just finished a staff meeting, so we can talk. Please keep it fairly short; there's another appointment coming up.
[seg_0003] Advisor (23.59-30.98): Certainly, I'll keep things concise. Let's start with the identification details for our telephone verification.
[seg_0004] Client (31.39-38.25): My FIN is G seven nine nine nine three zero six E. My date of birth is 7 February 1984.
[seg_0005] Advisor (38.65-45.81): Thank you. I've completed that check. You can tell me what you wanted to discuss today, and we'll take it from there.
[seg_0006] Client (46.21-58.49): The holding I want to reduce is Orion Global Income Fund. I was considering a reduction of 700 units. Also, telephone contact is still easiest for me. Coming down to the branch takes quite a bit of time out of the day.
[seg_0007] Advisor (58.89-69.17): Noted on the contact preference. We can arrange calls in advance rather than leave you waiting around. Has your office routine changed much since we last spoke?
[seg_0008] Client (69.58-79.78): Quite a bit, actually. I'm spending more mornings at home doing the consultancy paperwork, then coming into the office for meetings. The family has been sharing the administrative work more evenly.
[seg_0009] Advisor (80.19-88.61): That sounds like a different rhythm. For arranging our calls, should I continue contacting you directly rather than going through the office reception?
[seg_0010] Client (89.02-98.55): Yes, directly is better. Reception is busy with visiting clients, and messages sometimes reach me after I've left. A scheduled call is easier to fit between meetings.
[seg_0011] Advisor (98.95-118.33): All right, I'll note that contact arrangement. Turning to the disclosures now. For Orion Global Income Fund, rising market interest rates can push down the value of the bonds it holds, which can also lower its unit value. Do you understand how rising interest rates can lower the fund's unit value?
[seg_0012] Client (118.73-125.38): Yes, I understand. If interest rates rise, the bonds can fall in value and bring the fund's unit value down.
[seg_0013] Advisor (125.78-130.16): Thank you. I recommend selling Orion Global Income Fund.
[seg_0014] Client (130.56-134.21): Okay, noted. I want to sell, not add to the holding.
[seg_0015] Advisor (134.60-154.83): I'll cover the remaining disclosures now. The transaction charge is 0.25% of the sale proceeds. You could lose some or all of the capital you invested in this fund, and selling may realise a loss. Are you willing to accept investment losses, including a loss realised when reducing this holding?
[seg_0016] Client (155.23-160.27): Yes, I am willing to accept investment losses, including a realised loss on this reduction.
[seg_0017] Advisor (160.67-165.35): Thank you. I'm ready to record the remaining details whenever you're ready.
[seg_0018] Client (165.75-180.49): Use Singapore dollars as the transaction currency. Set the transaction amount at 150,000. For the order quantity, use the number of units I mentioned earlier. Place it as a limit order, with the limit price at 214.3 Singapore dollars.
[seg_0019] Advisor (180.89-187.36): Give me a moment while I finish entering that. I'll stay on the line; there's no need for you to call back.
[seg_0020] Client (187.76-194.97): No problem. I've still got a little time. It's much easier doing this directly than trying to coordinate a visit around everyone's diary.
[seg_0021] Advisor (195.37-214.52): Please confirm your final instruction: sell 700 units of Orion Global Income Fund, with a transaction amount of 150,000 in Singapore dollars, using a limit order at a limit price of 214.3 Singapore dollars. Is that the instruction you want me to execute?
[seg_0022] Client (214.92-219.60): Yes, I confirm that final instruction exactly as you have stated it. Please proceed.
[seg_0023] Advisor (220.00-230.28): Thank you, Elaine. I'll attend to the processing and the usual documentation. That's all I need from you on this call. I'll let you get back to your day.
[seg_0024] Client (230.68-235.38): Thanks, Adrian. Appreciate you keeping the call brief. Have a good afternoon.

the sales of riskier products to these clients. Instances were also noted where clients were 
told by their RMs that the risk profiling exercise was a paper exercise. These observations 
reflect RMs’ lack of risk consciousness and adopting a perfunctory approach towards the 
risk profiling exercise. MAS expects PBs to inculcate the right mindset and understanding 
amongst front office staff with regard to clients’ safeguards and their duty to act in the 
interest of their clients. PBs should pay  attention to changes in clien ts’ profiles and 
implement controls to mitigate the risk of clients being unduly influenced to take on 
higher risk profiles or invest in products beyond their intended risk appetites. Examples of 
such controls include regular analyses of migration of clients’ profiles to identify unusual 
trends and patterns, and perform ance of independent sampling checks (e.g. listening to 
voice logs) to assess whether RMs inappropriately influenced clients to adopt a higher risk 
tolerance.

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
